insight_1.title: Framework Explains Why History Repeats

insight_1.implication: This isn't random - it's structural; framework reveals the structure

insight_2.title: The Cost Multiplier Holds Across History
insight_2.observation: Wrong decisions cost 7-10x more to fix than right decisions would have cost to implement
evidence: Germ theory: Accept early (+cost) vs fix deaths late (-cost 500K+ lives)
Energy: Renewables early (+cost) vs transition now (-cost $2T+ assets)
AI: Safety research (+cost) vs restrict deployment (-cost = unknown but large)
insight_2.implication: Framework's 7-10x multiplier isn't arbitrary - it's consistent with actual history

insight_3.title: Bad Decisions Become Invisible Infrastructure
insight_3.observation: Wrong decisions embed themselves in systems, making reversal exponentially expensive
examples: Coal plants locked in → can't switch to renewables without stranded assets
AI scaled without safety → can't retrain without massive cost
Medical practice built on miasma → retraining entire profession
insight_3.implication: Early decisions are most important because they lock in costs for decades

insight_4.title: Resistance is Built Into Wrong Decisions

examples: Medical establishment fought germ theory for 20 years
Fossil fuel industry fights renewables transition
AI labs resist safety focus (capability is 'easier')
insight_4.implication: Resistance = sign of transition between wrong and right; framework predicts when it occurs
